purpose: Colour controls for matching the 1912 print's tone to the 1899 companion sheet. Presentation stage only - never applied to master_full.tif or any archival scan.

measured.method: print-to-print at 150 dpi: both PDFs rendered, page margins and water excluded; paper = modal colour (3-level quantisation), ink = mean of the darkest 0.3% by luminance. NOT master-to-print: the master's pre-JPEG blacks (9.8,6.8,6.6) are far deeper than any print black, and fitting across that mismatch would lift the blacks and wash out type.

levels.model: per-channel affine y = gain*x + offset, anchored so 1912 ink maps to 1899 ink and 1912 paper to 1899 paper. Per-channel (not 3x3) per the least-complex-model rule: a full 3x3 improved anchor RMS only 12.9 -> 9.6 while allowing channel mixing, i.e. hue shifts.
levels.black_check: master near-black (9.8,6.8,6.6) maps to (2.6,3.7,-3.9) pre-clip - blacks stay black

shoulder.why: a hard levels stretch to the 1899 paper level clips 15.3% of map content to 255; with the knee, 0.00% clips (swept K=200/210/220 on a 3125x3750 master slab; 210 keeps p99 at 233.9 vs the no-knee 244.3 with 2.93% clipped)

chroma.axis: Rec.601 luma; only distance from neutral changes, hue and luminance untouched
chroma.why: fitted optimum across paper/yellow/pink anchors (sweep: 1.00 -> mean err 9.0, 1.30 -> 6.6, 1.75 -> 10.3); the 1912 fills are ~2x less saturated than the 1899's at the same hues

orange_carveout.why: the 1899 has no orange class to match: connected components >= 2000 px at 150 dpi give the 1899 two pale-tan blobs (0.080% of page, one building, median 203,172,120) vs nineteen genuinely orange on the 1912 (0.448%, median 160,130,88). An earlier 'orange in both' reading was scattered blend pixels between yellow and pink fills. Orange therefore takes the brightness lift (levels+shoulder) but keeps its own saturation.

pink_wash_boost.why: owner-requested final match of the red/pink building class to the 1899 for side-by-side framing. Measured print-to-print at 150 dpi on the selected print(4): the LIGHT PINK WASH (V>=210, 86% of the class) is the only subclass off - median S 0.286 vs the 1899's 0.302 (ratio 0.947, needs x1.056); the mid (0.306 vs 0.294) and deep-red (0.357 vs 0.373) subclasses already match within tolerance and must not move. Hence the value ramp (HSV V = max channel of the post-transform pixel, the same statistic the subclasses were measured with; the first implementation ramped on Rec.601 luma, whose value for the wash is ~187, so the boost never engaged - caught by the slab test): full boost above V 215, zero below 190, so mid and deep tones are untouched. Gated by (1 - orange weight) so the D-016 orange hold is never double-treated. Luma-preserving chroma-only, like the main chroma step: hue and luminance untouched, legibility contrast unchanged by construction.
pink_wash_boost.why_per_region: D-022, owner report: the block-682 pink (sheet 9) reads lighter than its neighbours. Measured per source region on the print: the pink WASH varies by PLATE - s12 0.275, s09 0.286, s10/s43 0.294, s08 0.314, s39 0.318, s07 0.325, s11 0.345 - against the 1899's 0.302. Verified pre-existing in the archival master (s09 wash S 0.180 vs s11 0.227 untreated), i.e. plate inking variation, not a treatment artefact. Following the D-017 precedent (per-plate paper flat-field), each region's wash is brought to the common 1899 target 0.302: gains up for the pale plates (s12 x1.161 total, s09 x1.113) and down for the rich ones (s11 x0.923, s07 x0.980). Regions with no measurable pink (s40, s44, s49, s50, panels) keep the global 1.055. Confinement identical to D-021: pink band, value ramp, orange gate, luma preserved.
